newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ESTES THROWS TWO-HIT SHUTOUT AS GIANTS EDGE CARDS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ESTES THROWS TWO-HIT SHUTOUT AS GIANTS EDGE CARDS.

text.p: Shawn Estes threw his second two-hit shutout in just under a month and Jose Vizcaino drove in one run and scored another as the San Francisco Giants edged the St Louis Cardinals 2-0 Friday.

Estes (6-2), who also threw a two-hit shutout against the Astros on April 26, allowed just a pair of singles, walking three and striking out five. He didn't allow a runner to reach third base and retired the final 16 batters he faced in bouncing back from his worst start of the season.
"Tonight was loud," said Estes. "The people were into it and that gave us more adrenaline.
"I wanted to prove to the team, more than anything, that that was not the real me in Chicago. I couldn't wait to get back on the mound tonight. It was a long four days."
"It was a well played game," said Giants manager Dusty Baker. "We played good defence, that's our secret.

"Estes was more determined tonight than usual after his last start in Chicago. He was outstanding. He's a high-energy type of guy, a guy with a lot of pride. I figured he would come out with a strong game after Chicago."
Vizcaino doubled and scored on a Barry Bonds groundout in the fourth and drove in the Giants' final run in the sixth with a single that scored Stan Javier, who had singled and stolen second.
St Louis starter Matt Morris (1-3) pitched well, allowing two runs -- one earned -- and five hits over eight innnings, walking two and striking out seven.
"Both pitchers pitched very well but Estes got the better results," said Cardinals manager Tony La Russa.

In Los Angeles, John Smoltz allowed just two runs over eight innings and Ryan Klesko hit a two-run homer in the sixth as the Atlanta Braves defeated the Dodgers 4-2 for their seventh straight victory.
Smoltz (6-3) scattered seven hits, walked one and struck out five to win his fourth consecutive decision. He evened his career mark against Los Angeles at 11-11.
Mark Wohlers pitched the ninth to notch his 11th save.
Pedro Astacio (3-3) fell to 0-9 lifetime against Atlanta.
The Dodgers suffered their season-high sixth straight loss.

At Colorado, Dante Bichette hit a two-run homer and drove in three runs and Ellis Burks and Jason Bates also homered for the Rockies, helping rookie Bobby Jones to his first major-league victory, 8-7 over the Houston Astros.
Jones (1-0) went 6 2/3 innings, allowing six runs and 11 hits with two walks and no strikeouts. Steve Reed pitched a perfect ninth for his fourth save of the season.
Donne Wall (1-2) was tagged for eight runs and seven hits over 4 1/3 innings for the Astros, who have lost four of their last five games.
In Philadelphia, rookie Garrett Stephenson allowed just three hits over six innings as the Phillies beat New York 2-1.

Stephenson (2-0) yielded one run, walking three and striking out four. In his three major-league starts, the right-hander has allowed just three earned runs in 20 innings, striking out 20 and walking only five.
The Mets got their only run in the second on Bernard Gilkey's fourth homer.
In Montreal, Pedro Martinez matched a career-high with 12 strikeouts in his third complete game this season, a five-hitter that gave the Expos a 4-1 victory over Pittsburgh Pirates.

Martinez (8-0) did not allow a walk as he who became the second eight-game winner in the National League, joining Bobby Jones of the Mets. He lowered his league-leading ERA to 1.17. In 61 1/3 innings this season, the right-hander has allowed just eight earned runs.
Darrin Fletcher drove in two runs for Montreal, which snapped its three-game losing streak.

In San Diego, Fernando Valenzuela pitched 5 2/3 scoreless innings to snap a personal five-game losing streak and Wally Joyner hit a two-run homer as the Padres defeated the Florida Marlins 6-3 for their season-high fifth straight win.
Valenzuela (2-6) allowed five hits, walked two and struck out four for his first win since April 16.
San Diego has won six of its last seven.
Alex Fernandez (5-5) took the loss as Florida dropped its second straight game after winning nine in a row.

In Cincinnati, Terry Mulholland allowed five hits in eight innings for his fourth straight win and Sammy Sosa homered as the Chicago Cubs won for the fourth time in five games, defeating the Reds 3-1.
Mulholland (4-3) yielded one run, walked two and struck out one before giving way to Terry Adams, who worked a hitless ninth for his fourth save.
